format_bounds.rationale: 1 MiB is a new-format-only input and parser ceiling: it is generous relative to Lockspire-generated values (43-byte secret, 35-byte client ID), limits decode/allocation work, and does not narrow legacy helper inputs. The total bound is derived exactly from the 1 MiB secret plus 6-byte version/length/age prefix, 16-byte migrated timestamp/deadline suffix, 12-byte IV, 16-byte GCM tag, unpadded Base64URL expansion, and maximum 32-byte key ID. Oversized existing legacy values are not normalized, truncated, or fallback-read; migration/activation reports blocked and leaves them unchanged.

cases.lifecycle: generated credentials and explicit caller-provided helper inputs

cases.expected: new dedicated format accepts client_id and secret up to 1,048,576 bytes each; no legacy helper cap is added. Existing helper currently accepts arbitrary binary secret input for sealing and rejects empty/malformed on read. Generated secret is 32 random bytes encoded as 43 unpadded Base64URL chars; generated ID is `ls_` + 24 random bytes encoded as 32 chars (35 total). The envelope maximum is the formula-derived 1,398,207 ASCII bytes; parser checks encoded length before decoding and decoded lengths before allocation/use
